source.text: Πρωΐας δὲ γενομένης συμβούλιον ἔλαβον πάντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὥστε θανατῶσαι αὐτόν·

records.literal_gloss: Morning then having come, counsel took all the chief priests and the elders of the people against the Jesus so as to put to death him;

en.L: Now when morning had come, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus, so as to put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death;
en.B: Early in the morning all the chief priests and the elders of the people met and reached their decision against Jesus: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must be put to death.
en.R: Early the next morning, all the leading priests and the elders of the people met together. They made a plan to have Jesus killed.

es.L: Y llegada la mañana, todos los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos del pueblo tomaron consejo contra Jesús, para darle muerte;
es.B: Muy de mañana, todos los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos del pueblo se reunieron y tomaron su decisión contra Jesús: tenía que morir.
es.R: Temprano a la mañana siguiente, todos los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos del pueblo se reunieron. Planearon cómo hacer que mataran a Jesús.

sw.L: Na asubuhi ilipofika, wakuu wote wa makuhani na wazee wa watu walifanya shauri dhidi ya Yesu ili wamuue;
sw.B: Asubuhi na mapema wakuu wote wa makuhani na wazee wa watu walikutana, wakafikia uamuzi dhidi ya Yesu: lazima auawe.
sw.R: Kesho yake asubuhi na mapema, wakuu wote wa makuhani na wazee wa watu walikutana pamoja. Walipanga jinsi ya kumfanya Yesu auawe.

decisions.choice: took counsel: came to a decision together
decisions.reason: The phrase means to form a plan or reach a decision (12:14). After the hearing at night (26:57-68), the leaders now settle on their course.

decisions.choice: so as to put him to death: they needed the Roman governor to carry out the sentence
decisions.reason: Under Roman rule the Jewish council could not lawfully carry out an execution (John 18:31). So they took Jesus to Pilate (27:2).

decisions.choice: the next morning
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that this is the morning after the night hearing of chapter 26.

decisions.choice: los jefes de los sacerdotes; los ancianos del pueblo
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani; wazee wa watu
decisions.reason: The terms used for these groups throughout Matthew, recorded once in this passage.

source.text: καὶ δήσαντες αὐτὸν ἀπήγαγον καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ τῷ ἡγεμόνι.

records.literal_gloss: and having bound him they led away and handed over to Pilate the governor.

en.L: and having bound {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away and handed [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] over to Pilate the governor.
en.B: They tied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up, led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away, and handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to Pilate, the governor.
en.R: They tied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} up and led {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away. Then they handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over to Pilate, the Roman governor.

es.L: y, después de atarlo, [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] llevaron y [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] entregaron a Pilato, el gobernador.
es.B: Lo ataron, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaron a Pilato, el gobernador.
es.R: Lo ataron y se {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} llevaron. Luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaron a Pilato, el gobernador romano.

sw.L: na wakiisha kumfunga, walimpeleka, wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato mkuu wa mkoa.
sw.B: Walimfunga, wakamchukua, wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato, mkuu wa mkoa.
sw.R: Walimfunga, wakampeleka. Kisha wakamkabidhi kwa Pilato, mkuu wa mkoa wa Kirumi.

decisions.choice: Pilate the governor: Pontius Pilate, Roman governor of Judea
decisions.reason: Pilate governed Judea for Rome from about AD 26 to 36. Only he could order an execution.

decisions.choice: handed over: the verb used all through for Jesus being given up
decisions.reason: Jesus had said he would be handed over to the chief priests and then to the Gentiles (17:22; 20:18-19). Both now happen.

decisions.choice: Pilate, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Pontius Pilate, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts give his full name, Pontius Pilate. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Roman governor
decisions.reason: Readable says whose governor Pilate was.

decisions.choice: entregar, for every handing over of Jesus in the passage (27:2, 3, 18, 26); traicionar for Judas at Balanced (27:3)
decisions.reason: The same verb runs through the story of Jesus being given up (meaning decision m2), so Spanish keeps one verb, as the English keeps "handed over". Only Judas's act at Balanced is called betrayal, as in the English.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns, pronouns before the verb and possessives (lo, le, ti, él, su)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the end of the verb ("atarlo", "acusándolo"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise; a pronoun that begins a sentence is capitalised either way. So the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: kukabidhi for every handing over of Jesus in the passage (27:2, 3, 18, 26); kumsaliti for Judas at Balanced (27:3)
alternatives: kumtoa for Judas at Literal, as in John
decisions.reason: The same verb runs through the story of Jesus being given up (meaning decision m2), and Matthew's Judas uses it of himself in 27:4, so Swahili keeps the one verb used in John for this chain. Only Judas's act at Balanced is called betrayal, as in the English.

decisions.choice: mkuu wa mkoa (L, B); mkuu wa mkoa wa Kirumi (R)
decisions.reason: Pilate governed Judea for Rome (meaning decision m1). "Mkuu wa mkoa" (head of a province) is the plain standard term, used for him in John 18-19; "gavana" is a loanword used in only some countries, and "liwali" is an older coastal title. Readable says whose governor he was, as the English does. The same through the passage.

source.text: Τότε ἰδὼν Ἰούδας ὁ παραδιδοὺς αὐτὸν ὅτι κατεκρίθη μεταμεληθεὶς ἔστρεψεν τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια τοῖς ἀρχιερεῦσιν καὶ πρεσβυτέροις λέγων· Ἥμαρτον παραδοὺς αἷμα ἀθῷον.

records.literal_gloss: Then having seen Judas the [one] handing over him that he was condemned, having regretted he returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders \v 4 saying, I sinned having handed over blood innocent.

en.L: Then Judas, the one who handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over, seeing that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had been condemned, regretted [it] and brought back the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders, \v 4 saying, "I have sinned in handing over innocent blood."
en.B: When Judas, who had betrayed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saw that Jesus had been condemned, he was seized with regret and took the thirty silver coins back to the chief priests and the elders. \v 4 "I have sinned," he said. "I have handed an innocent man over to death."
en.R: Judas was the one who had handed Jesus over to the leaders. When he saw that Jesus had been sentenced to death, he felt terrible about what he had done. He took the thirty silver coins back to the leading priests and the elders. \v 4 He said, "I have sinned. I handed over a man who did nothing wrong, and now they will kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

es.L: Entonces Judas, el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregaba, viendo que había sido condenado, lleno de remordimiento devolvió las treinta piezas de plata a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a [los] ancianos, \v 4 diciendo: «He pecado entregando sangre inocente».
es.B: Cuando Judas, el que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} había traicionado, vio que Jesús había sido condenado, se llenó de remordimiento y devolvió las treinta monedas de plata a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los ancianos. \v 4 «He pecado», dijo. «He entregado a la muerte a un hombre inocente».
es.R: Judas era el que había entregado a Jesús a los dirigentes. Cuando vio que habían condenado a Jesús a muerte, se sintió muy mal por lo que había hecho. Devolvió las treinta monedas de plata a los jefes de los sacerdotes y a los ancianos. \v 4 Les dijo: «He pecado. Entregué a un hombre que no hizo nada malo, y ahora {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} van a matar».

sw.L: Kisha Yuda, yule aliyemkabidhi, alipoona kwamba amehukumiwa, alijuta, akavirudisha vile vipande thelathini vya fedha kwa wakuu wa makuhani na wazee, \v 4 akisema, "Nimetenda dhambi kwa kuikabidhi damu isiyo na hatia."
sw.B: Yuda, aliyekuwa amemsaliti, alipoona kwamba Yesu amehukumiwa, alijawa na majuto, akavirudisha vile vipande thelathini vya fedha kwa wakuu wa makuhani na wazee. \v 4 Akasema, "Nimetenda dhambi. Nimemkabidhi mtu asiye na hatia auawe."
sw.R: Yuda ndiye aliyekuwa amemkabidhi Yesu kwa viongozi. Alipoona kwamba Yesu amehukumiwa kifo, alijisikia vibaya sana kwa yale aliyoyafanya. Akazirudisha zile sarafu thelathini za fedha kwa wakuu wa makuhani na wazee. \v 4 Akasema, "Nimetenda dhambi. Nimemkabidhi mtu asiyekosa chochote, na sasa watamuua."

decisions.choice: regretted: was filled with remorse
decisions.reason: The verb means to feel sorry afterward about what one has done. It is not the word for repentance in 3:2 and 4:17; Matthew uses it of a change of mind in 21:29, 32. Judas regrets his act, but the story does not say he turned to God.

decisions.choice: innocent blood: the life of an innocent person, given up to death
decisions.reason: Blood stands for a life taken by violence. The law puts a curse on anyone who takes a bribe to kill an innocent person (Deuteronomy 27:25).

decisions.choice: the thirty pieces of silver: the sum agreed in 26:15
decisions.reason: The coins were most likely silver shekels or coins of the same weight. Thirty was the price the law set for a slave (Exodus 21:32), about four months' wages for a laborer.

decisions.choice: innocent, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: righteous, the reading of some manuscripts
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "righteous blood". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: who had betrayed him (B); handed Jesus over (R); handed an innocent man over to death (B)
alternatives: handed him over at every level
decisions.reason: The same verb means to hand over and, of a friend, to betray. Balanced calls Judas the betrayer, as 10:4 does, and says plainly what handing over innocent blood meant.

decisions.choice: thirty silver coins
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the coins. The value is given in a meaning decision.

decisions.choice: lleno de remordimiento (L), se llenó de remordimiento (B), se sintió muy mal (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is regret, remorse (meaning decision m1), not the word for repentance, which Spanish renders "arrepentirse" throughout. "Remordimiento" keeps the two apart.

decisions.choice: alijuta (L), alijawa na majuto (B), alijisikia vibaya sana (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is regret, remorse (meaning decision m1), not the word for repentance, which Swahili renders "kutubu" throughout. "Kujuta" keeps the two apart.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς;

records.literal_gloss: They but said, What to us?

en.L: But they said, "What [is that] to us?
en.B: They answered, "Why should that concern us?
en.R: But they said, "We do not care about that.

es.L: Pero ellos dijeron: «¿Qué [es eso] para nosotros?
es.B: Ellos respondieron: «¿Y a nosotros qué nos importa?
es.R: Pero ellos dijeron: «Eso no nos importa.

sw.L: Lakini wao walisema, "Linatuhusu nini sisi?
sw.B: Walimjibu, "Hilo linatuhusu nini?
sw.R: Lakini wao walisema, "Hilo halituhusu.

decisions.choice: What is that to us: that is no concern of ours
decisions.reason: The question is a way of refusing. The leaders who paid Judas will take no share in his guilt.

decisions.choice: a statement
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into the statement it means.

source.text: σὺ ὄψῃ.

records.literal_gloss: You will see.

en.L: You will see [to it]."
en.B: That is your affair."
en.R: That is your problem."

es.L: Tú verás».
es.B: Eso es asunto tuyo».
es.R: Ese es tu problema».

sw.L: Wewe utaona."
sw.B: Hilo ni shauri lako."
sw.R: Hiyo ni shida yako."

decisions.choice: you will see to it: deal with it yourself
alternatives: a prediction that Judas will see something
decisions.reason: The future is used as a command: the matter is yours. Pilate says the same words to the crowd in 27:24.

decisions.choice: That is your affair (B); That is your problem (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom.

source.text: καὶ ῥίψας τὰ ἀργύρια εἰς τὸν ναὸν ἀνεχώρησεν, καὶ ἀπελθὼν ἀπήγξατο.

records.literal_gloss: And having thrown the pieces of silver into the temple he withdrew, and having gone away he hanged himself.

en.L: And throwing the pieces of silver into the temple, he left; and he went away and hanged himself.
en.B: Judas flung the silver into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
en.R: Judas threw the money into the temple and left. Then he went off and hanged himself.

es.L: Y arrojando las piezas de plata en el templo, se retiró; y yéndose, se ahorcó.
es.B: Judas arrojó la plata en el templo y se marchó. Luego se fue y se ahorcó.
es.R: Judas tiró el dinero dentro del templo y se fue. Después se fue a otro lugar y se ahorcó.

sw.L: Na akivitupa vile vipande vya fedha ndani ya hekalu, aliondoka; na akienda zake, alijinyonga.
sw.B: Yuda alivitupa vile vipande vya fedha ndani ya hekalu, akaondoka. Kisha akaenda, akajinyonga.
sw.R: Yuda aliitupa ile fedha ndani ya hekalu, akaondoka. Kisha akaenda mahali pengine, akajinyonga.

decisions.choice: into the temple: the word usually means the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: Matthew's word usually means the sanctuary building, where only priests went. Judas may have thrown the coins into the court of the priests, or the word may be used loosely for the temple. Matthew does not say.

decisions.choice: he hanged himself: Matthew's account of Judas's death
decisions.reason: Acts 1:18-19 tells of Judas's death in other words and also speaks of a field called the Field of Blood. The text does not say how the two accounts fit together.

decisions.choice: the silver (B); the money (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable avoid repeating the full phrase from 27:3.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς λαβόντες τὰ ἀργύρια εἶπαν· Οὐκ ἔξεστιν βαλεῖν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν κορβανᾶν, ἐπεὶ τιμὴ αἵματός ἐστιν·

records.literal_gloss: The but chief priests having taken the pieces of silver said, Not it is lawful to put them into the treasury, since price of blood it is;

en.L: But the chief priests took the pieces of silver and said, "It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is [the] price of blood."
en.B: The chief priests gathered up the coins. "The law does not let us put this into the temple treasury," they said, "because it was paid to bring about a death."
en.R: The leading priests picked up the money. They said, "Our law does not allow us to put this money in the temple treasury. It was paid to have a man killed."

es.L: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes, tomando las piezas de plata, dijeron: «No es lícito echarlas en el tesoro, puesto que es precio de sangre».
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes recogieron las monedas. «La ley no nos permite ponerlas en el tesoro del templo», dijeron, «porque se pagaron para causar una muerte».
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes recogieron el dinero. Dijeron: «Nuestra ley no nos permite poner este dinero en el tesoro del templo. Se pagó para que mataran a un hombre».

sw.L: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani, wakivichukua vile vipande vya fedha, walisema, "Si halali kuviweka katika hazina, kwa kuwa ni bei ya damu."
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani waliviokota vile vipande vya fedha, wakasema, "Sheria hairuhusu tuviweke katika hazina ya hekalu, kwa sababu vimelipwa ili mtu auawe."
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani waliichukua ile fedha. Wakasema, "Sheria yetu hairuhusu tuweke fedha hii katika hazina ya hekalu. Ililipwa ili mtu auawe."

decisions.choice: the treasury: the temple fund for offerings
decisions.reason: The word comes from the term for a gift given to God (Mark 7:11). The law forbade bringing money gained by sin into God's house as an offering (Deuteronomy 23:18).

decisions.choice: price of blood: money paid for a killing
decisions.reason: The phrase means the price paid to take a life. The priests speak of the money in the very terms Judas used in 27:4, though they had paid it themselves.

decisions.choice: paid to bring about a death (B); paid to have a man killed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idiom means.

source.text: συμβούλιον δὲ λαβόντες ἠγόρασαν ἐξ αὐτῶν τὸν Ἀγρὸν τοῦ Κεραμέως εἰς ταφὴν τοῖς ξένοις.

records.literal_gloss: Counsel then having taken they bought with them the Field of the Potter for burial for the strangers.

en.L: So after taking counsel, they bought with them the Potter's Field as a burial place for strangers.
en.B: They talked it over and decided to buy the Potter's Field with the money, as a place to bury people from other lands.
en.R: They decided to use the money to buy a field known as the Potter's Field. It would be a place to bury people from other places who died in Jerusalem.

es.L: Y después de tomar consejo, compraron con ellas el Campo del Alfarero, como sepultura para los extranjeros.
es.B: Lo hablaron entre ellos y decidieron comprar con ese dinero el Campo del Alfarero, como lugar para enterrar a gente de otras tierras.
es.R: Decidieron usar el dinero para comprar un terreno conocido como el Campo del Alfarero. Sería un lugar para enterrar a la gente de otros lugares que moría en Jerusalén.

sw.L: Basi wakiisha kufanya shauri, walinunua kwa vipande hivyo Shamba la Mfinyanzi, liwe mahali pa kuwazika wageni.
sw.B: Walishauriana, wakaamua kununua Shamba la Mfinyanzi kwa fedha hiyo, liwe mahali pa kuwazika watu wa nchi nyingine.
sw.R: Waliamua kutumia fedha hiyo kununua shamba lililojulikana kama Shamba la Mfinyanzi. Lingekuwa mahali pa kuwazika watu kutoka sehemu nyingine waliofia Yerusalemu.

decisions.choice: the Potter's Field: a field known by that name
alternatives: any field owned by a potter
decisions.reason: The article shows a known place, perhaps where potters dug clay or worked. The name prepares for the quotation in 27:10.

decisions.choice: strangers: people from elsewhere, such as visitors and foreigners who died in the city
decisions.reason: The word means people who do not belong to the place. Pilgrims and foreigners who died in Jerusalem had no family grave there.

decisions.choice: people from other places who died in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable explains who the strangers were.

source.text: διὸ ἐκλήθη ὁ ἀγρὸς ἐκεῖνος Ἀγρὸς Αἵματος ἕως τῆς σήμερον.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore was called the field that Field of Blood until the today.

en.L: Therefore that field has been called [the] Field of Blood to this day.
en.B: This is why that field has had the name Field of Blood ever since, up to the present day.
en.R: That is why people still call that place the Field of Blood.

es.L: Por eso aquel campo ha sido llamado Campo de Sangre hasta hoy.
es.B: Por esta razón aquel campo se llama Campo de Sangre desde entonces hasta el día de hoy.
es.R: Por eso la gente todavía llama a ese lugar el Campo de Sangre.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo shamba lile limeitwa Shamba la Damu hadi leo.
sw.B: Ndiyo sababu shamba hilo limekuwa likiitwa Shamba la Damu tangu wakati huo hadi leo.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu watu bado wanaliita mahali pale Shamba la Damu.

decisions.choice: Field of Blood: named for the blood money that bought it
decisions.reason: The field was bought with the price of Jesus's death (27:6). Acts 1:19 gives the name in Aramaic, Hakeldama, and explains it from Judas's death.

decisions.choice: to this day: to the time when Matthew wrote
alternatives: to the day of the crucifixion
decisions.reason: The phrase tells the first readers that the name was still in use in their own time (compare 28:15).

source.text: τότε ἐπληρώθη τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἰερεμίου τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος· Καὶ ἔλαβον τὰ τριάκοντα ἀργύρια, τὴν τιμὴν τοῦ τετιμημένου ὃν ἐτιμήσαντο ἀπὸ υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ, καὶ ἔδωκαν αὐτὰ εἰς τὸν ἀγρὸν τοῦ κεραμέως, καθὰ συνέταξέν μοι κύριος.

records.literal_gloss: Then was fulfilled the [thing] spoken through Jeremiah the prophet saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the [one] having been priced, whom they priced from sons of Israel, \v 10 and they gave them for the field of the potter, as directed me Lord.

en.L: Then what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying, "And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who had been priced, on whom [some] of [the] sons of Israel set a price, \v 10 and they gave them for the potter's field, as [the] Lord directed me."
en.B: Then the word spoken through the prophet Jeremiah was fulfilled: "They took the thirty silver coins, the price set on the one whose value some of the people of Israel had fixed, \v 10 and they gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord had instructed me."
en.R: This made what the prophet Jeremiah had said come true: "They took the thirty silver coins. That was the price some of the people of Israel put on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 10 They used the coins to buy the potter's field, as the Lord had told me."

es.L: Entonces se cumplió lo dicho por medio del profeta Jeremías, cuando dijo: «Y tomaron las treinta piezas de plata, el precio del que fue tasado, a quien tasaron [algunos] de [los] hijos de Israel, \v 10 y las dieron por el campo del alfarero, como me ordenó [el] Señor».
es.B: Así se cumplió lo que había dicho el profeta Jeremías: «Tomaron las treinta monedas de plata, el precio puesto a aquel cuyo valor fijaron algunos del pueblo de Israel, \v 10 y las dieron por el campo del alfarero, como el Señor me había mandado».
es.R: Así se cumplió lo que había dicho el profeta Jeremías: «Tomaron las treinta monedas de plata. Ese fue el precio que algunos del pueblo de Israel pusieron por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. \v 10 Usaron las monedas para comprar el campo del alfarero, como el Señor me había dicho».

sw.L: Ndipo likatimia lile lililonenwa kupitia nabii Yeremia, akisema, "Nao walivichukua vile vipande thelathini vya fedha, bei ya yule aliyewekewa bei, ambaye [baadhi] ya wana wa Israeli walimwekea bei, \v 10 nao walivitoa kwa ajili ya shamba la mfinyanzi, kama Bwana alivyoniagiza."
sw.B: Hapo neno lililosemwa kupitia nabii Yeremia lilitimia: "Walivichukua vile vipande thelathini vya fedha, bei aliyowekewa yule ambaye baadhi ya watu wa Israeli walimkadiria thamani, \v 10 wakavitoa kwa ajili ya shamba la mfinyanzi, kama Bwana alivyokuwa ameniagiza."
sw.R: Jambo hili lilitimiza maneno aliyosema nabii Yeremia: "Walichukua zile sarafu thelathini za fedha. Hiyo ndiyo bei ambayo baadhi ya watu wa Israeli waliiweka juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. \v 10 Walizitumia sarafu hizo kununua shamba la mfinyanzi, kama Bwana alivyoniambia."

decisions.choice: spoken through Jeremiah: the words are closest to Zechariah 11:12-13, joined with themes from Jeremiah
decisions.reason: The thirty pieces of silver, the price set, and the money thrown to the potter in the temple come from Zechariah 11:12-13. Jeremiah goes to a potter's house (18:1-12), breaks a potter's jar at a valley to be renamed for slaughter and burial (19:1-13), and buys a field with silver (32:6-15). Matthew may name Jeremiah as the better-known prophet whose themes shape the combined words. Why he names only Jeremiah is not certain.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Zechariah, or no name, in a few manuscripts
decisions.reason: A few manuscripts read "Zechariah" or leave the name out, which looks like an attempt to ease the difficulty. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they took, they gave: the leaders are the ones who acted
alternatives: I took, I gave, as in Zechariah 11:13
decisions.reason: The first verb can mean "I took" or "they took". The SBLGNT reads "they gave" in 27:10, so the sentence reads best as the leaders' actions, which Matthew has just told. Some manuscripts read "I gave".

decisions.choice: as the Lord directed me: the Lord is God, whose name stands in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The closing words echo the way Scripture speaks of doing what God commanded. In Zechariah 11:13 the Hebrew has God's name, which the Greek Old Testament gives as "Lord".

decisions.choice: the people of Israel
decisions.reason: The phrase means Israelites. Literal keeps "sons"; those who set the price were men, so no setting applies.

decisions.choice: the price as a sentence of its own, with him for the one priced
alternatives: the price of the one who had been priced
decisions.reason: Readable breaks up the play on words and makes plain that the one priced is Jesus, so the pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: tasado, tasaron (L); el precio puesto, fijaron su valor (B)
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats one word for "price" three times (price, priced, set a price). Literal keeps the repetition with "precio" and "tasar", the verb for setting a price on something; Balanced spreads it over plainer words, as the English does.

decisions.choice: bei, aliyewekewa bei, walimwekea bei
decisions.reason: The Greek repeats one word for "price" three times. Literal keeps the repetition with "bei" (price) and "kuwekea bei" (to set a price on); "kuthamini" would also mean to value someone highly, the opposite of the contempt in the words.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐστάθη ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ ἡγεμόνος· καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ ἡγεμὼν λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus stood before the governor; and asked him the governor saying, You are the King of the Jews?

en.L: Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the King of the Jews?"
en.B: Jesus now stood in front of the governor, who questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the King of the Jews?"
en.R: Jesus stood in front of Pilate, the governor. Pilate asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the King of the Jews?"

es.L: Y Jesús estuvo de pie delante del gobernador; y el gobernador {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó, diciendo: «¿Tú eres el Rey de los judíos?».
es.B: Jesús estaba ahora de pie ante el gobernador, que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el Rey de los judíos?».
es.R: Jesús estaba de pie delante de Pilato, el gobernador. Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntó: «¿Eres {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} el Rey de los judíos?».

sw.L: Na Yesu alisimama mbele ya mkuu wa mkoa; na mkuu wa mkoa alimwuliza, akisema, "Wewe ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Yesu sasa alisimama mbele ya mkuu wa mkoa, naye akamwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Yesu alisimama mbele ya Pilato, mkuu wa mkoa. Pilato akamwuliza, "Je, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi?"

decisions.choice: the King of the Jews: a political charge
decisions.reason: Rome alone appointed kings. A man called king without Rome's approval was a rebel. The magi used the same title at Jesus's birth (2:2), and it will be the charge over the cross (27:37).

decisions.choice: you: stressed
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out: you, this prisoner, are the king?

decisions.choice: King, capitalized
decisions.reason: In this chapter the words are a title, the charge written over the cross (27:37), so King is capitalized at every level. Readable names Pilate.

decisions.choice: el Rey de los judíos, at every level; ¿Tú eres ...? (L), ¿Eres tú ...? (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at John 18:33: a title, and a political charge (meaning decision m1), so "Rey" takes a capital. Literal puts the stressed "tú" first, as the Greek does (meaning decision m2); at the start of the question it is written plain, elsewhere under the setting.

decisions.choice: Wewe ndiwe Mfalme wa Wayahudi, at every level
decisions.reason: As at John 18:33: the title names the nation and is a political charge (meaning decision m1). "Ndiwe" (you are the one) marks it as a title and carries the stress on "you" (meaning decision m2). At the head of the Literal question "Wewe" is capitalised either way and takes no span.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἔφη· Σὺ λέγεις.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus said, You say.

en.L: And Jesus said, "You say [so]."
en.B: Jesus replied, "It is you who say it."
en.R: Jesus answered, "You are the one saying that."

es.L: Y Jesús dijo: «Tú [lo] dices».
es.B: Jesús respondió: «Eres tú quien lo dice».
es.R: Jesús contestó: «Tú eres el que dice eso».

sw.L: Na Yesu alisema, "Wewe unasema [hivyo]."
sw.B: Yesu alijibu, "Wewe ndiye unayesema hivyo."
sw.R: Yesu alijibu, "Ni wewe unayesema hivyo."

decisions.choice: You say so: a guarded yes, which leaves the words in Pilate's mouth
decisions.reason: Jesus does not deny the title, but he does not take up Pilate's meaning either. He answered Judas and the high priest in a similar way, with the past tense of the same verb (26:25, 64). The kind of king Pilate fears is not what Jesus is.

decisions.choice: You: stressed, it is Pilate who says it
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out, putting weight on Pilate as the speaker. Jesus speaks to Pilate, so the pronoun takes no setting.

decisions.choice: It is you who say it (B); You are the one saying that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the guarded form of the answer and do not turn it into a plain yes.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ κατηγορεῖσθαι αὐτὸν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ πρεσβυτέρων οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο.

records.literal_gloss: And in the being accused him by the chief priests and elders nothing he answered.

en.L: And while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was being accused by the chief priests and elders, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered nothing.
en.B: But when the chief priests and the elders brought their charges against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made no reply.
en.R: The leading priests and the elders kept accusing {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said nothing in reply.

es.L: Y mientras era acusado por los jefes de los sacerdotes y [los] ancianos, nada respondió.
es.B: Pero cuando los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos presentaban sus acusaciones contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, no respondió nada.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos seguían acusándolo. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no respondió nada.

sw.L: Na alipokuwa akishtakiwa na wakuu wa makuhani na wazee, hakujibu lolote.
sw.B: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani na wazee walipotoa mashtaka yao dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, hakujibu neno.
sw.R: Wakuu wa makuhani na wazee waliendelea kumshtaki. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakusema chochote kujibu.

decisions.choice: he answered nothing: perhaps Isaiah 53:7
decisions.reason: The servant in Isaiah 53:7 was silent like a sheep before its shearers. Jesus was silent before the council too (26:63). Matthew does not cite the verse here.

decisions.choice: while he was being accused: the charges went on
decisions.reason: The construction describes the accusing as it went on, perhaps charge after charge (27:13).

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yeye, yake, chake, wewe)
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("alipokuwa akishtakiwa", "wamkabidhi"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting covers fewer words than in English. This applies to the whole passage.

source.text: τότε λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Οὐκ ἀκούεις πόσα σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;

records.literal_gloss: Then says to him the Pilate, Not do you hear how many things against you they testify?

en.L: Then Pilate says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not hear how many things they testify against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.B: Then Pilate said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not hear all the charges they are bringing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.R: So Pilate said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "They are accusing {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} of so many things. Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} not hear them?"

es.L: Entonces Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «¿No oyes cuántas cosas testifican contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».
es.B: Entonces Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¿No oyes todas las acusaciones que presentan contra {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}?».
es.R: Por eso Pilato {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «Te acusan de muchísimas cosas. ¿No las oyes?».

sw.L: Kisha Pilato anamwambia, "Husikii ni mambo mangapi wanayoshuhudia dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?"
sw.B: Kisha Pilato alimwambia, "Husikii mashtaka yote haya wanayoleta dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}?"
sw.R: Basi Pilato alimwambia, "Wanakushtaki kwa mambo mengi sana. Husikii?"

decisions.choice: testify against: bring evidence against, accuse
decisions.reason: The verb is used of witnesses giving evidence against someone in court, as at the night hearing (26:62).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal (dice); pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this passage in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Spanish narrative does. The same in 27:22.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal (anamwambia); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Matthew tells parts of this passage in the present. Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the narrative past, with -li- for the first verb and -ka- for those that follow. The same in 27:22.

source.text: καὶ οὐκ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ πρὸς οὐδὲ ἓν ῥῆμα, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν ἡγεμόνα λίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And not he answered him to not even one word, so as to marvel the governor greatly.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not answer him, not even to one word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
en.B: Still Jesus did not answer him on even one point, and the governor was deeply amazed at this.
en.R: But Jesus did not say one word to answer him. The governor was very surprised.

es.L: Y no le respondió ni a una sola palabra, de modo que el gobernador se asombraba mucho.
es.B: Pero Jesús no le respondió ni a un solo cargo, y el gobernador quedó muy asombrado.
es.R: Pero Jesús no dijo ni una palabra para responderle. El gobernador estaba muy sorprendido.

sw.L: Naye hakumjibu hata neno moja, hata mkuu wa mkoa akastaajabu sana.
sw.B: Hata hivyo Yesu hakumjibu hata shtaka moja, na mkuu wa mkoa alishangaa sana.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu hakusema neno lolote kumjibu. Mkuu wa mkoa alishangaa sana.

decisions.choice: word: point or charge
decisions.reason: The noun can mean a word or a matter. Jesus did not answer a single one of the charges.

decisions.choice: the governor was amazed: Jesus's silence surprised him
decisions.reason: Prisoners facing death usually defended themselves. Jesus's silence left Pilate wondering.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since the sentence before ended with Pilate speaking.

source.text: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν εἰώθει ὁ ἡγεμὼν ἀπολύειν ἕνα τῷ ὄχλῳ δέσμιον ὃν ἤθελον.

records.literal_gloss: At now feast was accustomed the governor to release one to the crowd prisoner whom they wanted.

en.L: Now at [the] feast the governor was accustomed to release to the crowd one prisoner, whom they wanted.
en.B: At each festival the governor used to set free one prisoner for the crowd, whichever one they wanted.
en.R: Each year at the Passover festival, the governor would let one prisoner go free. The crowd could choose which prisoner it would be.

es.L: Y en [la] fiesta el gobernador acostumbraba soltar a la multitud un preso, el que quisieran.
es.B: En cada fiesta el gobernador solía dejar en libertad a un preso para la multitud, el que ellos quisieran.
es.R: Cada año, en la fiesta de la Pascua, el gobernador dejaba libre a un preso. La gente podía escoger qué preso sería.

sw.L: Na wakati wa sikukuu mkuu wa mkoa alikuwa na desturi ya kuufungulia umati mfungwa mmoja, yule waliyemtaka.
sw.B: Kila sikukuu mkuu wa mkoa alikuwa na desturi ya kumwachilia huru mfungwa mmoja kwa ajili ya umati, yeyote waliyemtaka.
sw.R: Kila mwaka wakati wa sikukuu ya Pasaka, mkuu wa mkoa alikuwa akimwachilia huru mfungwa mmoja. Watu waliweza kuchagua mfungwa yupi aachiliwe.

decisions.choice: the feast: the Passover
decisions.reason: The story has been set at the Passover since 26:2. The custom belonged to this feast.

decisions.choice: the release of a prisoner: a custom known only from the Gospels
decisions.reason: No other ancient writer mentions this custom, but all four Gospels do (Mark 15:6; John 18:39). It was a favor to the people at their festival.

decisions.choice: Each year at the Passover festival
decisions.reason: Readable names the feast and makes the yearly custom clear.

source.text: εἶχον δὲ τότε δέσμιον ἐπίσημον λεγόμενον Ἰησοῦν Βαραββᾶν.

records.literal_gloss: They were having then at that time a prisoner notorious called Jesus Barabbas.

en.L: And at that time they had a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.
en.B: At that time they were holding a prisoner everyone knew of, called Jesus Barabbas.
en.R: At that time there was a well-known prisoner named Jesus Barabbas.

es.L: Y tenían entonces un preso notorio llamado Jesús Barrabás.
es.B: En ese tiempo tenían un preso que todos conocían, llamado Jesús Barrabás.
es.R: En ese tiempo había un preso muy conocido, llamado Jesús Barrabás.

sw.L: Na wakati huo walikuwa na mfungwa mmoja mwenye sifa mbaya aitwaye Yesu Baraba.
sw.B: Wakati huo walikuwa wamemfunga mfungwa mmoja aliyejulikana na kila mtu, aitwaye Yesu Baraba.
sw.R: Wakati huo kulikuwa na mfungwa mmoja aliyejulikana sana, aitwaye Yesu Baraba.

decisions.choice: Jesus Barabbas, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Barabbas, the reading of most manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts have only "Barabbas" here and in 27:17. A few manuscripts and some early translations read "Jesus Barabbas", and the SBLGNT follows them. Jesus was a common name, and copyists were more likely to drop it from a criminal than to add it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Barabbas: an Aramaic name meaning son of the father
decisions.reason: Bar means son and abba means father. It was a family name. Mark 15:7 says he was held with rebels who had committed murder.

decisions.choice: notorious: well known, here for his crimes
decisions.reason: The word means marked out or famous. Mark 15:7 and Luke 23:19 tell of rebellion and murder.

decisions.choice: a prisoner everyone knew of (B); a well-known prisoner (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for a prisoner whose name was widely known.

decisions.choice: mwenye sifa mbaya (L); aliyejulikana na kila mtu (B); aliyejulikana sana (R)
decisions.reason: The man was well known for his crimes (meaning decision m3). "Mashuhuri" and "maarufu" are words of praise in Swahili, so Literal says "of bad reputation", and Balanced and Readable say only that he was well known, as the English does.

source.text: συνηγμένων οὖν αὐτῶν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν, Ἰησοῦν τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἢ Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν;

records.literal_gloss: Having been gathered therefore of them said to them the Pilate, Whom do you want I release to you, Jesus the Barabbas or Jesus the [one] called Christ?

en.L: So when they had gathered, Pilate said to them, "Whom do you want me to release to you, Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus, the [one] called {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"
en.B: When the crowd had gathered, Pilate asked them, "Which one do you want me to set free for you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}?"
en.R: So when the people had come together, Pilate asked them, "Which man do you want me to set free? Should it be Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus, the one people call {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}?"

es.L: Así que, estando ellos reunidos, Pilato les dijo: «¿A quién {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} suelte: a Jesús Barrabás o a Jesús, el llamado {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.B: Cuando la multitud se reunió, Pilato les preguntó: «¿A cuál {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} deje en libertad: a Jesús Barrabás, o a Jesús, al que llaman {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}?».
es.R: Cuando la gente se reunió, Pilato les preguntó: «¿A qué hombre {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que deje libre? ¿A Jesús Barrabás, o a Jesús, al que la gente llama {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}?».

sw.L: Basi walipokuwa wamekusanyika, Pilato aliwaambia, "Mnataka niwafungulie nani, Yesu Baraba, au Yesu aitwaye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.B: Umati ulipokusanyika, Pilato aliwauliza, "Mnataka nimwachilie huru yupi kwa ajili yenu: Yesu Baraba, au Yesu anayeitwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.R: Basi watu walipokusanyika, Pilato aliwauliza, "Mnataka nimwachilie huru mtu yupi? Je, ni Yesu Baraba, au Yesu, yule ambaye watu humwita {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"

decisions.choice: Jesus Barabbas, as in 27:16
alternatives: Barabbas, the reading of most manuscripts
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts read only "Barabbas" here too; see the note at 27:16. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: who is called Christ: Pilate repeats what others say of Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 1:16 the phrase gives the name people know him by. Pilate does not say he believes it.

decisions.choice: two men named Jesus set side by side
decisions.reason: If the SBLGNT reading is right, the crowd must choose between two men named Jesus: one called son of the father, the other called the Messiah.

decisions.choice: the one people call
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the title is what people were saying about Jesus.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans on every plural "you" (quieren|queréis, les|os)
decisions.reason: Spanish has two plural forms of "you", Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; the setting chooses between them. English has no such choice, so these spans have no English counterpart. The same throughout the passage.

source.text: ᾔδει γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παρέδωκαν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: He knew for that because of envy they had handed over him.

en.L: For he knew that it was out of envy that they had handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over.
en.B: He was aware that envy had moved them to hand Jesus over.
en.R: Pilate knew that the leaders had brought Jesus to him because they were jealous of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Porque sabía que por envidia {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} habían entregado.
es.B: Él sabía que la envidia los había llevado a entregar a Jesús.
es.R: Pilato sabía que los dirigentes le habían llevado a Jesús porque {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenían envidia.

sw.L: Kwa maana alijua kwamba walimkabidhi kwa sababu ya wivu.
sw.B: Alifahamu kwamba wivu ndio uliowasukuma kumkabidhi Yesu.
sw.R: Pilato alijua kwamba viongozi walikuwa wamemleta Yesu kwake kwa sababu walimwonea wivu.

decisions.choice: envy: resentment of the following Jesus had among the people
decisions.reason: The leaders had feared the crowds who held Jesus to be a prophet (21:46) and resented the praise he received (21:15-16).

decisions.choice: they: the chief priests and elders
decisions.reason: Those who handed Jesus over were the leaders (27:1-2).

decisions.choice: the leaders
decisions.reason: Readable says who handed Jesus over.

source.text: Καθημένου δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ λέγουσα· Μηδὲν σοὶ καὶ τῷ δικαίῳ ἐκείνῳ, πολλὰ γὰρ ἔπαθον σήμερον κατ’ ὄναρ δι’ αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Sitting then of him on the judgment seat sent to him the wife of him saying, Nothing to you and to the righteous that; many things for I suffered today in a dream because of him.

en.L: Now while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent [word] to him, saying, "[Have] nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered many things today in a dream because of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: As Pilate sat on the judgment seat, a message came to him from his wife: "Leave that righteous man alone. Today in a dream I went through great distress over {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: Pilate was sitting in his place as judge. While he was there, his wife sent him a message. It said, "Do not have anything to do with that man. He is innocent. Today I had a dream about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and it troubled me very much."

es.L: Y estando él sentado en el tribunal, le envió [recado] su mujer, diciendo: «[No tengas] nada que ver con ese justo, porque hoy he sufrido mucho en sueños por causa de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.B: Mientras Pilato estaba sentado en el tribunal, su esposa le mandó un mensaje: «Deja en paz a ese hombre justo. Hoy, en un sueño, he sufrido mucho por causa de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}».
es.R: Pilato estaba sentado en el asiento del juez. Mientras estaba allí, su esposa le mandó un mensaje que decía: «No tengas nada que ver con ese hombre. Es inocente. Hoy tuve un sueño sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y me angustió mucho».

sw.L: Na alipokuwa ameketi katika kiti cha hukumu, mke wake alimtumia [ujumbe], akisema, "[Usiwe na] jambo lolote na yule mwenye haki, kwa maana leo nimeteseka mengi katika ndoto kwa ajili {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.B: Pilato alipokuwa ameketi katika kiti cha hukumu, mke wake alimtumia ujumbe: "Mwache yule mtu mwenye haki. Leo nimeteseka sana katika ndoto kwa sababu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}."
sw.R: Pilato alikuwa ameketi kwenye kiti cha hakimu. Alipokuwa pale, mke wake alimtumia ujumbe uliosema, "Usijihusishe na mtu yule. Hana hatia. Leo nimeota ndoto juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, nayo imenisumbua sana."

decisions.choice: the judgment seat: the raised platform where a Roman official sat to give judgment
decisions.reason: Pilate is acting as judge in a formal hearing.

decisions.choice: righteous: innocent, in the right
decisions.reason: In a court the word means one who is in the right and not guilty. Pilate's wife declares Jesus innocent, as Pilate himself soon claims to be (27:24).

decisions.choice: a dream: a warning sent in a dream
decisions.reason: Matthew tells of God guiding people by dreams (1:20; 2:12, 13, 19, 22). Here the dream warns of Jesus's innocence. Matthew does not say what she saw.

decisions.choice: He is innocent
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense the word has in a court. The pronoun begins a sentence, so it is written plain.

decisions.choice: sent [word]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies what she sent.

decisions.choice: el tribunal (L, B); el asiento del juez (R)
decisions.reason: As at John 19:13: Spanish "tribunal" names both a court and the raised seat from which a judge gives sentence (meaning decision m1); Readable says plainly what the seat was for.

decisions.choice: kiti cha hukumu (L, B); kiti cha hakimu (R)
decisions.reason: As at John 19:13: the raised seat from which a Roman official gave judgment (meaning decision m1). Readable says it was the judge's seat.

decisions.choice: mwenye haki
decisions.reason: "Righteous" here means innocent, in the right (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep "mwenye haki", the key term for righteousness; Readable says "Hana hatia" (he is innocent), as the English Readable does.

source.text: Οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι ἔπεισαν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα αἰτήσωνται τὸν Βαραββᾶν τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν ἀπολέσωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: The but chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds that they should ask for the Barabbas, the but Jesus they should destroy.

en.L: But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus.
en.B: But the chief priests and the elders talked the crowds into asking for Barabbas and having Jesus put to death.
en.R: But the leading priests and the elders talked the people into asking Pilate to free Barabbas and to have Jesus killed.

es.L: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos persuadieron a las multitudes para que pidieran a Barrabás y destruyeran a Jesús.
es.B: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos convencieron a la multitud de que pidiera a Barrabás e hiciera matar a Jesús.
es.R: Pero los jefes de los sacerdotes y los ancianos convencieron a la gente para que le pidieran a Pilato que soltara a Barrabás y que mataran a Jesús.

sw.L: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani na wazee waliyashawishi makundi ya watu ili wamwombe Baraba, na Yesu wamwangamize.
sw.B: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani na wazee waliwashawishi watu wamwombe Baraba na Yesu auawe.
sw.R: Lakini wakuu wa makuhani na wazee waliwashawishi watu wamwombe Pilato amwachilie Baraba na Yesu auawe.

decisions.choice: destroy: have him put to death
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy or kill. The crowds could only ask; Pilate would give the order.

decisions.choice: the crowds: the people gathered at the governor's residence
decisions.reason: Matthew speaks of the crowds present that morning, whom the leaders persuaded. This shapes how 27:25 should be read.

decisions.choice: having Jesus put to death (B); to have Jesus killed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what destroying him meant.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ ἡγεμὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τίνα θέλετε ἀπὸ τῶν δύο ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Answering then the governor said to them, Whom do you want from the two I release to you?

en.L: And the governor answered and said to them, "Which of the two do you want me to release to you?"
en.B: The governor asked them again, "Which of these two do you want me to set free for you?"
en.R: The governor asked the people, "Which of these two men do you want me to set free?"

es.L: Y respondiendo el gobernador, les dijo: «¿A cuál de los dos {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} suelte?».
es.B: El gobernador les volvió a preguntar: «¿A cuál de estos dos {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que {{plural_you:les|os}} deje en libertad?».
es.R: El gobernador le preguntó a la gente: «¿A cuál de estos dos hombres {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} que deje libre?».

sw.L: Na mkuu wa mkoa, akijibu, aliwaambia, "Kati ya hawa wawili mnataka niwafungulie yupi?"
sw.B: Mkuu wa mkoa aliwauliza tena, "Kati ya hawa wawili, mnataka nimwachilie huru yupi kwa ajili yenu?"
sw.R: Mkuu wa mkoa aliwauliza watu, "Kati ya watu hawa wawili, mnataka nimwachilie yupi?"

decisions.choice: answered: responded to the situation, not to a question
decisions.reason: The word often introduces speech without a question before it (11:25). Pilate responds to the crowd's growing pressure.

decisions.choice: again
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that Pilate is repeating the question of 27:17.

source.text: οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Τὸν Βαραββᾶν.

records.literal_gloss: They but said, The Barabbas.

en.L: And they said, "Barabbas."
en.B: "Barabbas!" they said.
en.R: They answered, "Barabbas!"

es.L: Y ellos dijeron: «A Barrabás».
es.B: «¡A Barrabás!», dijeron.
es.R: Ellos respondieron: «¡A Barrabás!».

sw.L: Nao walisema, "Baraba."
sw.B: "Baraba!" walisema.
sw.R: Walijibu, "Baraba!"

decisions.choice: Barabbas: the name alone
decisions.reason: From here on the SBLGNT, like all manuscripts, uses only the name Barabbas. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

source.text: λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Τί οὖν ποιήσω Ἰησοῦν τὸν λεγόμενον χριστόν;

records.literal_gloss: Says to them the Pilate, What then shall I do [with] Jesus the [one] called Christ?

en.L: Pilate says to them, "Then what shall I do with Jesus, the [one] called {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"
en.B: Pilate asked them, "Then what am I to do with Jesus who is called {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}?"
en.R: Pilate asked, "Then what should I do with Jesus, the one people call {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}?"

es.L: Pilato les dice: «¿Qué haré, pues, con Jesús, el llamado {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.B: Pilato les preguntó: «Entonces, ¿qué hago con Jesús, al que llaman {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}?».
es.R: Pilato preguntó: «Entonces, ¿qué debo hacer con Jesús, al que la gente llama {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}?».

sw.L: Pilato anawaambia, "Basi nimfanye nini Yesu aitwaye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.B: Pilato aliwauliza, "Basi nimfanye nini Yesu anayeitwa {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.R: Pilato aliuliza, "Basi nimfanye nini Yesu, yule ambaye watu humwita {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"

decisions.choice: what shall I do: a real question for the crowd
decisions.reason: Pilate puts the decision in the crowd's hands, as he will again in 27:24.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: λέγουσιν πάντες· Σταυρωθήτω.

records.literal_gloss: They say all, Let him be crucified.

en.L: They all say, "Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be crucified!"
en.B: They all shouted, "Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be crucified!"
en.R: All of them shouted, "Have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} killed on a cross!"

es.L: Dicen todos: «¡Sea crucificado!».
es.B: Todos gritaron: «¡Que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucifiquen!».
es.R: Todos gritaron: «¡Que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} maten en una cruz!».

sw.L: Wote wanasema, "Asulubiwe!"
sw.B: Wote walipiga kelele, "Asulubiwe!"
sw.R: Wote walipiga kelele, "Auawe msalabani!"

decisions.choice: crucified: put to death on a cross
decisions.reason: Crucifixion was the Roman death for slaves and rebels. It was slow and shameful, carried out in public as a warning. Jesus had foretold it (20:19).

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: Have him killed on a cross
decisions.reason: Readable says what crucifixion was.

decisions.choice: ¡Sea crucificado! (L); ¡Que lo crucifiquen! (B); ¡Que lo maten en una cruz! (R); also 27:23
decisions.reason: The Greek is a passive command, "let him be crucified". Literal keeps the passive; Balanced and Readable use the impersonal "que lo ...", the natural Spanish way to call for something to be done to someone. "¡Crucifícalo!" would make Pilate the one addressed, as in John 19:6 where the Greek says so. Readable says what crucifying is (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Asulubiwe (L, B); Auawe msalabani (R); also 27:23
decisions.reason: The Greek is a passive command, "let him be crucified", and the Swahili passive subjunctive says exactly that. "Msulubishe" would make Pilate the one addressed, as in John 19:6 where the Greek says so. Readable says what crucifying is (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἔφη· Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν;

records.literal_gloss: The but said, What for evil did he do?

en.L: But he said, "Why, what evil has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done?"
en.B: "But what wrong has {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} done?" Pilate asked.
en.R: Pilate asked, "Why? What bad thing has this man done?"

es.L: Pero él dijo: «Pues ¿qué mal ha hecho?».
es.B: «Pero ¿qué mal ha hecho?», preguntó Pilato.
es.R: Pilato preguntó: «¿Por qué? ¿Qué cosa mala ha hecho este hombre?».

sw.L: Naye alisema, "Kwa nini, amefanya ubaya gani?"
sw.B: "Lakini amefanya kosa gani?" Pilato aliuliza.
sw.R: Pilato aliuliza, "Kwa nini? Mtu huyu amefanya jambo gani baya?"

decisions.choice: for: a word of protest, why, what then
decisions.reason: In a question the word adds force: why, what has he done?

decisions.choice: Pilate
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker.

source.text: οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Σταυρωθήτω.

records.literal_gloss: They but all the more were crying out saying, Let him be crucified.

en.L: But they kept crying out all the more, saying, "Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be crucified!"
en.B: But they only shouted louder and louder, "Let {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} be crucified!"
en.R: But the people shouted even louder, "Have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} killed on a cross!"

es.L: Pero ellos gritaban aún más, diciendo: «¡Sea crucificado!».
es.B: Pero ellos gritaban cada vez más fuerte: «¡Que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucifiquen!».
es.R: Pero la gente gritó todavía más fuerte: «¡Que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} maten en una cruz!».

sw.L: Lakini wao walizidi kupiga kelele, wakisema, "Asulubiwe!"
sw.B: Lakini wao walizidi kupaza sauti, "Asulubiwe!"
sw.R: Lakini watu walipiga kelele kwa nguvu zaidi, "Auawe msalabani!"

decisions.choice: kept crying out all the more: the shouting grew and went on
decisions.reason: The tense shows a shout repeated again and again, growing louder.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ Πιλᾶτος ὅτι οὐδὲν ὠφελεῖ ἀλλὰ μᾶλλον θόρυβος γίνεται λαβὼν ὕδωρ ἀπενίψατο τὰς χεῖρας ἀπέναντι τοῦ ὄχλου λέγων· Ἀθῷός εἰμι ἀπὸ τοῦ αἵματος τούτου· ὑμεῖς ὄψεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: Having seen then the Pilate that nothing it avails but rather a riot is arising, having taken water he washed the hands before the crowd saying, Innocent I am of the blood this; you will see.

en.L: And when Pilate saw that he was gaining nothing, but rather a riot was starting, he took water and washed [his] hands before the crowd, saying, "I am innocent of this blood; you will see [to it]."
en.B: Pilate saw that he was getting nowhere and that an uproar was starting instead. So he took water and washed his hands in front of the crowd. "I am not guilty of this man's death," he said. "That is your affair."
en.R: Pilate saw that he could not change their minds. Instead, the crowd was starting to riot. So he took some water and washed his hands in front of them. He said, "I am not to blame for this man's death. You are responsible for it."

es.L: Y viendo Pilato que nada lograba, sino que más bien se formaba un tumulto, tomando agua, se lavó las manos delante de la multitud, diciendo: «Inocente soy de esta sangre; {{plural_you:ustedes verán|vosotros veréis}}».
es.B: Pilato vio que no conseguía nada y que, en cambio, se estaba formando un alboroto. Entonces tomó agua y se lavó las manos delante de la multitud. «No soy culpable de la muerte de este hombre», dijo. «Es asunto {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestro}}».
es.R: Pilato vio que no podía hacerles cambiar de opinión. Al contrario, la gente estaba empezando a alborotarse. Así que tomó agua y se lavó las manos delante de ellos. Dijo: «Yo no tengo la culpa de la muerte de este hombre. {{plural_you:Ustedes son|Vosotros sois}} los responsables».

sw.L: Na Pilato, alipoona kwamba hafaulu kitu, bali ghasia inaanza, alichukua maji, akanawa mikono mbele ya umati, akisema, "Sina hatia ya damu hii; ninyi mtaona."
sw.B: Pilato aliona kwamba hapati mafanikio yoyote, bali badala yake fujo zilikuwa zinaanza. Basi alichukua maji, akanawa mikono mbele ya umati, akasema, "Sina hatia juu ya kifo cha mtu huyu. Hilo ni shauri lenu."
sw.R: Pilato aliona kwamba hangeweza kubadilisha mawazo yao. Badala yake, watu walikuwa wanaanza kufanya fujo. Basi alichukua maji, akanawa mikono mbele yao. Akasema, "Mimi sina lawama kwa kifo cha mtu huyu. Ninyi ndio mnaohusika."

decisions.choice: washing the hands: a sign of declaring oneself innocent of a death
decisions.reason: The law gives this act to the elders of a town after an unsolved killing (Deuteronomy 21:6-9), and the psalms speak of washing the hands in innocence (Psalm 26:6; 73:13). Pilate uses a sign the crowd would understand.

decisions.choice: this blood: the blood of this man
decisions.reason: The words can be read "this blood" or "the blood of this man". Either way they mean Jesus's death.

decisions.choice: of this blood, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: of the blood of this righteous man, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "of the blood of this righteous man", echoing 27:19. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you will see to it: the responsibility is yours
decisions.reason: Pilate uses the words the priests used to Judas in 27:4, and passes the matter to the crowd. Washing his hands does not undo his own order (27:26).

decisions.choice: not guilty of this man's death (B); not to blame for this man's death (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly what the idiom of blood means.

decisions.choice: ustedes verán (L); Es asunto de ustedes (B)
decisions.reason: Pilate turns on the crowd the words the chief priests used to Judas in 27:4 ("Tú verás", "Eso es asunto tuyo"); the responsibility is theirs (meaning decision m4). Literal and Balanced repeat the wording of 27:4 so that the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: ninyi mtaona (L); Hilo ni shauri lenu (B)
decisions.reason: Pilate turns on the crowd the words the chief priests used to Judas in 27:4 ("Wewe utaona", "Hilo ni shauri lako"); the responsibility is theirs (meaning decision m4). Literal and Balanced repeat the wording of 27:4 so that the echo can be heard.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πᾶς ὁ λαὸς εἶπεν· Τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς καὶ ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα ἡμῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And answering all the people said, The blood of him on us and on the children of us.

en.L: And all the people answered and said, "His blood [be] on us and on our children!"
en.B: All the people there answered, "Let the guilt for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death fall on us and on our children!"
en.R: All the people there shouted back, "We and our children will take the blame for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} death!"

es.L: Y respondiendo todo el pueblo, dijo: «¡Su sangre [sea] sobre nosotros y sobre nuestros hijos!».
es.B: Todo el pueblo que estaba allí respondió: «¡Que la culpa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte caiga sobre nosotros y sobre nuestros hijos!».
es.R: Toda la gente que estaba allí le gritó: «¡Nosotros y nuestros hijos cargaremos con la culpa de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} muerte!».

sw.L: Na watu wote wakajibu, wakasema, "Damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} [na iwe] juu yetu na juu ya watoto wetu!"
sw.B: Watu wote waliokuwa pale walijibu, "Hatia ya kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} na iwe juu yetu na juu ya watoto wetu!"
sw.R: Watu wote waliokuwa pale walimjibu kwa kelele, "Sisi na watoto wetu tutabeba lawama ya kifo {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}!"

decisions.choice: his blood be on us: we accept the guilt for his death
alternatives: a wish to be cleansed by his blood
decisions.reason: The phrase takes on responsibility for a death (2 Samuel 1:16; Jeremiah 26:15; Acts 5:28). The crowd answers Pilate's claim to be innocent of this blood (27:24).

decisions.choice: the cry of this crowd at that moment
alternatives: a curse on the Jewish people for all time
decisions.reason: The words are the shout of the crowd gathered before Pilate that morning, whom their leaders had persuaded (27:20). Matthew reports what they said. The verse has been used to blame the Jewish people as a whole for Jesus's death and to justify hatred of Jews; the text does not support that use. Jesus, his disciples and the women at the cross were Jews, and in Matthew Jesus's blood is poured out for the forgiveness of sins for many (26:28).

decisions.choice: all the people: those present who answered Pilate
decisions.reason: Matthew here uses the word "people", often used of Israel, in place of "crowd". The context limits it to those who stood before Pilate and answered him. Some read the change of word as making the crowd stand for the nation; the sentence itself speaks of those present.

decisions.choice: Let the guilt for his death fall on us (B); take the blame for his death (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means. Literal keeps the words of the cry.

decisions.choice: there
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the people are those present.

decisions.choice: Damu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}
alternatives: Damu yake written plain, as the English "His blood"
decisions.reason: The English writes "His" plain because it begins the sentence. In Swahili the possessive follows the noun, so it is not sentence-initial and takes the reader setting, as at John 18:36.

source.text: τότε ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, τὸν δὲ Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας παρέδωκεν ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: Then he released to them the Barabbas, the but Jesus having flogged he handed over that he might be crucified.

en.L: Then he released Barabbas to them, but after having Jesus flogged, he handed [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] over to be crucified.
en.B: So Pilate let Barabbas go free, as they wanted. As for Jesus, Pilate ordered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be scourged, and then handed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} over for crucifixion.
en.R: Then Pilate set Barabbas free for the people. He had his soldiers beat Jesus with whips. Then he handed Jesus over to be killed on a cross.

es.L: Entonces les soltó a Barrabás, pero a Jesús, después de hacerlo azotar, [{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}] entregó para que fuera crucificado.
es.B: Así que Pilato dejó libre a Barrabás, como querían. En cuanto a Jesús, Pilato mandó que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} azotaran, y luego {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} entregó para que fuera crucificado.
es.R: Entonces Pilato soltó a Barrabás para la gente. Mandó a sus soldados que azotaran a Jesús. Después entregó a Jesús para que lo mataran en una cruz.

sw.L: Kisha aliwafungulia Baraba, lakini Yesu, akiisha kumpigisha mijeledi, alimkabidhi ili asulubiwe.
sw.B: Basi Pilato alimwachilia huru Baraba, kama walivyotaka. Kuhusu Yesu, Pilato aliamuru apigwe mijeledi, kisha akamkabidhi ili asulubiwe.
sw.R: Kisha Pilato aliwafungulia watu Baraba. Akawaamuru askari wake wampige Yesu mijeledi. Kisha akamkabidhi Yesu ili auawe msalabani.

decisions.choice: flogged: beaten with a Roman whip
decisions.reason: The Roman whip had leather straps weighted with bits of bone or metal. Flogging came before crucifixion and left the victim badly weakened. Jesus had foretold it (20:19).

decisions.choice: handed over: the verb used all through for Jesus being given up
decisions.reason: Judas handed him to the leaders, the leaders handed him to Pilate (27:2), and now Pilate hands him over to death, as Jesus had said (20:18-19; 26:2).

decisions.choice: Pilate ordered (B); had his soldiers (R); as they wanted (B)
decisions.reason: Pilate gave the order; his soldiers did the flogging. Balanced and Readable say so.
